name: introduction-bullets
text: Discarded cigarettes, nascent flame and delayed smoke can precede serious fires. AI Fireguard investigates whether a compact vision detector can localise these hazards early enough to support human-verified alerts and future response planning.

name: method-evaluation-copy
text:
YOLOv5s · 7.02M parameters · legacy best.pt initialisation · all layers unfrozen

45 epochs | 640 × 640 | batch 8 | MPS | workers 2 | seed 0

2 h 04 min training | 2.82 GB max RSS | ~13.1 GB unified-memory footprint | 0 swaps | 14 MB model | 11.3 ms/image at batch 8

SYSTEM CONCEPT
CCTV / edge video → cigarette, flame and smoke boxes → confidence filtering → human verification → alert and route-planning interface.

EVIDENCE POLICY
Report split-integrity checks and independent-test metrics together. Do not treat the legacy validation artifact or a single inference image as deployment evidence.

Scope: detector evaluation only; escape-route integration remains a prototype concept.

name: evidence-boundary-band
text:
ERROR ANALYSIS + NEXT EXPERIMENTS

1  SMALL / OCCLUDED CIGARETTES
Add close-range and hand-occlusion examples; tune class-specific confidence and IoU thresholds.

2  FIRE-LIKE HARD NEGATIVES
Add lights, sunsets, reflections, fog, steam and low-light backgrounds; report false alarms per hour.

3  TEMPORAL + DOMAIN VALIDATION
Test frame-to-frame consistency, unseen buildings and cameras; measure alert latency and sustained-event recall.

4  SAFE SYSTEM INTEGRATION
Only human-verified detections should trigger the escape-route prototype; keep certified alarms as the primary safety layer.

name: section-V-Conclusion
text: V. Conclusion
textPreview: V. Conclusion

name: conclusion-bullets
text:
WHAT CHANGED
• Leakage auditing changed the scientific conclusion: the legacy checkpoint fell from an apparent validation AP50 of 0.889 to 0.084 on the independent clean test.

WHAT WORKED
• Retraining recovered AP50 to 0.755 and AP50–95 to 0.453 without cross-split leakage.
• Smoke achieved the strongest precision (0.919) and strict AP (0.595).

WHAT REMAINS
• Cigarette recall (0.634) is limited by small size and hand occlusion.
• Flame AP50–95 (0.360) indicates localisation error despite 0.740 recall.
• Missed targets dominate more than cross-class confusion.

DECISION
The detector is promising for human-verified early alerts. It is not ready for safety-critical autonomy until class calibration, temporal validation and unseen-building tests are completed.
